A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, traceable through the retained architecture, equations, experiments and illustrations despite renaming MotionBase to MotionLib. All pages and appendices are readable. Internal inconsistencies affect interpretation of particular results, not material completeness.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation, reconstruction, scaling, out-of-domain and ablation results in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds instruction-tuning, feature-design, training-strategy and caption-quality evaluations.

M1.justification: Beyond the retained autoregressive and 2D-LFQ design, v2 introduces SMPL-D135 motion features and a separate motion-instruction-tuning stage. The data pipeline replaces OSX extraction with WHAM and adds physics-based refinement, quality weighting and GPT-4o caption refinement.

E1.justification: The main corpus shifts from a mixture containing many repeated-image poses to dynamic motions, with substantial Kinetics-700, NTU-RGBD-120 and ActivityNet components absent from v1's source distribution. Static poses remain in appendix experiments, including a new static/synthetic evaluation set. HumanML3D, Motion-X and the UNSEEN-90K scenario remain.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds MotionGPT-v2, distinct from the previously included MotionGPT variants. Table 7 adds H2VQ's literature-reported Motion-X MPJPE of 62.34, and Table 13 compares T2M-GPT against the decoder-only model. Existing main comparators are retained, making this a limited extension.

E3.justification: New protocols include 900K instruction-tuning examples, motion-recovery FPS evaluation and text-only/visual-text caption scoring on a five-point scale. GPT-2's reported size changes from 700M to 355M without establishing a backbone replacement. The OOD training specification also changes but becomes ambiguous: Table 4 names 11 subsets while the prose still states 38.

E4.justification: v2 adds ablations of instruction tuning, motion features, hierarchical captions, LoRA versus full tuning, and encoder-decoder versus decoder-only architectures, plus caption-quality assessment. The static/synthetic study is substantially revised. Earlier loss-mask, evaluator and 1D-versus-2D analyses remain under reorganized appendix headings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Additional point estimates and caption-quality scores do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Scaling, OOD and static/synthetic results are substantially revised under changed settings, preventing straightforward between-version performance comparisons. Table 3 preserves the earlier Ours row as Being-M0-VQ and adds Being-M0-LFQ with R@1 0.528 and FID 0.141. The main reconstruction table changes 2D-LFQ's HumanML3D FID from 1.769 to 0.092, although v2 Appendix Table 14 retains 1.769.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the 135-dimensional motion representation, comprising nine root dimensions and 126 joint-rotation dimensions. The likelihood objective, binary LFQ rule and token-index formula remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 adds compact, lossless motion features as a central contribution and explicitly claims a first demonstration of data/model scaling laws for motion generation. Its advertised contributions center on MotionLib, MotionBook and Being-M0. Metric limitations and static/synthetic-data benefits remain discussed but cease to be headline claims.

C2.justification: v1 attributes Motion-X degradation to evaluator limitations; v2 interprets its revised results as evidence of beneficial pretraining initialization. v2 also tempers static/synthetic-data benefits to marginal gains, motivates feature selection through efficiency and information preservation, and adds explanations concerning LoRA capacity and refinement failures on drastic movements.

D1.justification: v2 supplies detailed feature layouts, instruction-template construction, tracking and filtering procedures, caption-rating instructions and a project-page link. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Existing hardware, learning rates, batch sizes and the 300-epoch schedule are largely retained and relocated to Appendix A.

R1.justification: The related-work framework remains centered on LLMs, quantization and motion generation. v2 adds HumanTomato, MotionGPT-v2, WHAM, physics-refinement and TMR references, while removing background references including WebVid and InternViD. Positioning additionally emphasizes lossless features and an explicit scaling-law novelty claim.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with new dataset/model terminology throughout. Dataset construction and experimental discussion are reorganized; convergence and metric-limitations discussions move into the appendix. Appendices are substantially restructured around implementation, dataset construction and experimental analyses.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws and moves the architecture diagram into the main text, revises dataset illustrations and distribution charts, and adds or expands tables. Figure 4 replaces v1's MPJPE plots with the retained appendix FID plots but labels them MPJPE; the same curves remain labeled FID in Figure 12.

improvement.justification: v2 improves method documentation and adds targeted training, feature and annotation-quality checks missing from v1. However, previously matching reconstruction results become unexplained discrepancies between Tables 7 and 14, Figure 4 mislabels retained FID curves as MPJPE, and the OOD protocol becomes inconsistent about 11 versus 38 training subsets. These problems affect central quantitative evidence, so the benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
